# SkillMe

> A philosophy-first protocol for analyzing any reported issue — software incident, complaint,
> conflict, policy question, research anomaly, everyday decision — as a finite, auditable
> retained difference instead of a guessed name, cause, or fix. Two-question intake gate,
> stakeholder-vs-agency mapping, bidirectional global+local evidence-challenged hypotheses, and
> a three-lane (Known-Direct / Cross-Adaptive / Generative-Transformative) candidate generator.
> Tier: `Dr` (design rationale) — see README's Tier honesty section before citing this as proof
> of anything beyond protocol structure.

Do not infer this project's maturity from the spec's length. Start at `AI_START_HERE.md` and
follow its discovery order before making any capability or correctness claim.

## Docs

- [AI_START_HERE.md](/AI_START_HERE.md): Start here — what this project is, the discovery
  order, and how to verify the kernel's self-test yourself.
- [README.md](/README.md): Full framing, tier-honesty statement, quickstart (Claude Code plugin
  install and standalone kernel usage), repository map, downstream tooling overview.
- [SKILLME.md](/SKILLME.md): The canonical,
  normative spec — thesis, root grammar (with verified external lineage to `readout_genesis`),
  entities, axioms, the full 20-phase protocol, the two-question intake gate, the domain-mapping
  method (§6.9.1-6.9.4), the hypothesis evidence challenge protocol, the three-lane candidate
  generator, 48 protocol invariants, and the development roadmap.
- [docs/FIELD_REFERENCE.md](/docs/FIELD_REFERENCE.md): Generated field-by-field reference for
  constructing a new checkpoint — which fields are actually kernel-enforced (not all of them),
  the 3 `review_mode` evidence vocabularies. Regenerate via `tools/generate_field_reference.py`
  after any kernel schema change; never hand-edit it.
- [plugins/skillme/skills/skillme/SKILL.md](/plugins/skillme/skills/skillme/SKILL.md):
  The operational summary an AI assistant loads and follows when actually applying the
  protocol to a reported issue.
- [doc_ecosystem_bridge/README.md](/doc_ecosystem_bridge/README.md): Bridges a checkpoint into a
  human-ai-doc-ecosystem project (logbook entries, open decisions, optional doc drafting).
- [communication_glossary/README.md](/communication_glossary/README.md): 4-layer pipeline
  (deterministic word graph -> AI-interpretive expert-framework layer -> issue-anchored
  glossary -> Human/AI-orchestrator/AI-doer/AI-auditor skill plan) for the shared vocabulary
  and role/skill plan two people from different fields need to discuss and act on one issue.
- [run_pipeline.py](/run_pipeline.py): One-command orchestrator over the 4-layer pipeline and
  doc_ecosystem_bridge/bridge.py — shells out to each script, does not reimplement their logic.
- [CHANGELOG.md](/CHANGELOG.md): Version history through v0.4.10; states which later roadmap
  milestones are not yet complete.

## Verification (run this yourself — do not take claims on trust)

- `python3 skillme_protocol_kernel.py --self-test`: 14 structural test cases (happy path +
  deliberate violation cases) against the reference kernel — stdlib only, no network.
- `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q`: pytest wrapper around the self-test plus demo/checkpoint-demo
  fixtures.
- `python3 skillme_protocol_kernel.py --print-demo` / `--print-checkpoint-demo`: prints the full
  `[SimulatedData]`-labeled example run records referenced throughout the spec and README.

## Install as a Claude Code skill

```
/plugin marketplace add morrocwi/skillme
/plugin install skillme@yaoharee-lahtee-skillme
```

## Scope note

This kernel validates protocol *structure* (required fields, enum validity, gate ordering,
cross-references) — it does not and cannot verify that any domain claim, cause, or fix
reported through the protocol is true. Treat `protocol_status: VALID` as "well-formed", not
"correct".
